sections.h2: Where in Delta County are deeds recorded?
sections.html:
Everything goes through Escanaba. The Register of Deeds works from the county building at 310 Ludington Street, open from eight to four, and the county line is (906) 789-5100, with a fax at (906) 789-5179.

That holds whether the house stands in Escanaba, in Gladstone, in the village of Garden, or out in a township near Rapid River or Rock. Phone ahead about anything unusual, bring the original signed deed and the fee, and ask whether cards are accepted.

The office follows the statewide schedule in MCL 600.2567, which applies unless a charter county sets its own. Under it a deed is $30 to record whatever the page count.

Recording fees for an Escanaba closing
ServiceFee
Recording one document$30.00
Each additional instrument in an assignment or discharge$3.00
Photocopies$1.00 a page
Certifying a recorded paper$5.00
Records search on request$0.50 for each year, minimum $5
Filing another paper$1.00

Pay when you hand the document over. The statute lets a document that is both filed and paid for electronically settle within one business day, so ask whether the office accepts e-recording and from which vendors.

sections.h2: What transfer tax comes out of a Delta County seller's proceeds?
sections.html:
Two charges: $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county on each $500 slice of price, a partial slice counting as whole. MCL 207.504 sets the county charge, and MCL 207.523 puts liability on the seller. The county treasurer collects, and the clock runs 15 days from the buyer's receipt of the deed.

  • State tax does not apply to transfers under $100, instruments given as security, land contracts that hold back title until paid, or conveyances to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • If tax was paid on a sale that later proves to have qualified for an exemption, the seller, or a buyer who paid for the seller, may request a refund from the Department of Treasury.
  • The deed must state its value, or an affidavit declaring the value must travel with it.

The county statute, MCL 207.505, carries a shorter exemption list. A family transfer can therefore escape the state share and still owe the county share, so ask the register before you sign.

sections.h2: Which deeds need a treasurer's certificate?
sections.html:
Most sale deeds do. Under MCL 211.135 the register must hold a deed, plat or land contract until the treasurer certifies tax liens and tax titles and confirms that five years of taxes are paid.

Quitclaims and other conveyances without warranty covenants are excused, as are sheriff's deeds and some state tax deeds. The county treasurer keeps county money, collects delinquent property taxes, certifies deeds and runs the annual tax sale for the State Treasury.

Ask the treasurer what the certificate costs and how quickly it is issued before you pick a closing date. If back taxes exist, obtain a written payoff so they can be satisfied from the seller's proceeds.

Title agents and appraisers lean on the Delta County Equalization office. Its price list shows a $5 Equalization Report, a $15 Apportionment Report listing millage rates, and $15 for taxable value broken out by school district or township. Database copies run $1 a page and simple maps $2.

A single house is different. For its assessed and taxable value, contact the assessor in the city or township where it sits. A buyer estimating the first tax bill will want those two numbers and the millage rate.

sections.h2: Delta County housing at a glance
sections.html:
The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $157,100, median rent is $692, and median household income is $57,809. Owners live in 82.0% of occupied homes. The county has about 36,582 residents spread over 1,171 square miles of land, so parcels range from city lots in Escanaba and Gladstone to farms and forest acreage.

For a seller the practical upshot is variety. A lakeside cottage near Escanaba, a house in Gladstone and forty acres near Garden call for different disclosures, surveys and legal descriptions, but all three travel to the same counter on Ludington Street for recording.

sections.h2: What formatting does a Delta County deed need?
sections.html:
Michigan applies a single recording format everywhere, found in MCL 565.201. Expect Delta County to enforce these items.

  • Ink signatures, with the name printed beneath each, and names that agree from body to notary block.
  • Street addresses for each party, plus who drafted the deed and where they can be reached.
  • An acknowledgment by a notary, judge or court clerk for a deed signed in Michigan.
  • A blank 2.5 inches at the head of page one for the recorder's stamp.
  • No more than four trailing digits of a Social Security number.

Counter staff neither write deeds nor give legal advice. For an inherited house, ask the title company whether a death certificate or court order must be recorded ahead of the deed.

faqs.q: How much does the Delta County register charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars a document, per MCL 600.2567. A release naming several instruments adds $3 for each extra, and certifying a recorded paper costs $5.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax on a Delta County house sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. The state rate is $3.75 and the county rate 55 cents for every $500 slice, payable to the county treasurer inside 15 days of delivery.

faqs.q: Do deeds for Gladstone and Garden homes go to Escanaba?
faqs.a: Yes. The register at 310 Ludington Street records for the entire county, including both cities and the village.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed exempt from the treasurer's certificate in Delta County?
faqs.a: Yes, when it has no warranty covenants. A warranty deed or land contract must carry the certificate before the register will accept it.

faqs.q: What are the register's hours in Escanaba?
faqs.a: Eight to four. Telephone (906) 789-5100 to confirm holiday closures.
